$comment: Durable record of the repository's reuse guardrails: what is enforced, by which tool, and why.
This file is documentation, not a rule engine — every rule below is enforced by the tool named
in its `enforcedBy` field. Changing this file alone changes nothing.
Do not edit this file, scripts/guardrails/*.json, or an ignore list to make a check pass.

rules.rule: Declared npm dependencies (both blocks) are a closed set; a new one fails until the baseline is rebased.
rules.why: checkr is a published single-package library; a new dependency adds supply-chain and maintenance surface to every consumer and must be a deliberate, named decision.

rules.rule: `process.env` keys read by src/ are a closed set.
rules.why: A library reading process.env at runtime ties behavior to deployment inputs. src/ reads none today. Warn-only: it should be noticed in review, not block a build.

rules.rule: A src/lib module may only import from its own layer and the layers below it (types < xml < xsd < validator, with core as the composition root). Importing upward (e.g. types importing xml) or outside the DAG (e.g. xsd importing benchmark) is a violation.
rules.canonicalTarget: the layer's own allowed set defined in scripts/guardrails.mjs LIB_LAYERS
rules.why: The DAG keeps the module graph navigable and prevents coupling where a lower layer would depend on a higher one. The layer map was derived from evidence (the actual imports the tree takes) and is the minimal set that captures the architecture's intended direction. An invariant, not an inventory: there is no baseline file, so `--update` cannot launder a violation.
rules.notes: Only the first segment after `@lib/` is checked. `@lib/types/xsd` is a `types` import — deeper paths stay within their layer. Dependencies (`@xmldom/xmldom`, node builtins) are not layer edges and are not checked.

rules.rule: No non-test src file may import a sibling via a relative specifier (`./` or `../`). All imports from the project itself must go through the `@lib/*` or `@benchmark/*` alias.
rules.why: Aliases keep files movable: an import survives a move because it names the module, not the location. Tests import their colocated sibling relatively — that is the deliberate, inherited pattern and is exempt.
rules.notes: Detects `from "./x"` / `from "../x"` specifiers. A bare side-effect `import "./x"` would be missed (there are none today). An invariant, not an inventory: there is no baseline file, so `--update` cannot launder a violation.

consideredAndRejected.reason: `@xmldom/xmldom` is imported by 14 non-test files across all layers (types, xml, xsd, validator). There is no single canonical wrapper — xml/parser.ts wraps DOMParser for XML parsing, but other files import the library directly for DOM types (Document, Element). Wrapping all usage is an ADR-scale change, not a guardrail.
Tests are colocated with their subject, so they import across layers freely. A test-layer rule would add noise without benefit — tests are already excluded from the invariant checks.
Benchmark files import from src/lib via `@lib/core/main` and from `@benchmark/utils` — both use aliases. No violation to enforce. If a relative import appears, source-relative-imports catches it.
